config.title: Build duplicate job prevention logic

intro.title: Build duplicate job prevention logic
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build duplicate job prevention logic to ensure that a job processing system doesn't handle the same task more than once. You'll learn to use a JavaScript Set data structure to track job IDs and check for duplicates efficiently. The core programming concept involves managing state with a Set and implementing conditional logic to skip duplicate jobs. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand basic data structures and control flow in Node.js.
intro.usecase: Duplicate job prevention is essential in task queue systems like Bull or Agenda, where identical jobs could waste resources or cause data corruption. This pattern appears in e-commerce platforms preventing duplicate order processing, in CI/CD pipelines ensuring unique build jobs, and in notification systems avoiding spam. Developers implement this in dashboard job monitors, admin panels with job submission forms, and automated workflow tools where users schedule recurring tasks. The logic prevents system overload and ensures data integrity when multiple triggers could create identical background jobs.

objectives: Initialize a data structure to track active job IDs.
Implement a function to check for duplicate job submissions.
Apply conditional logic to prevent duplicate job execution.
Manipulate the tracking structure upon job completion.
Integrate duplicate prevention into a job processing workflow.
Configure error handling for duplicate detection scenarios.

steps.title: Create helper function to read existing jobs
steps.instruction: Create a function named readExistingJobs that reads the job tracking file, parses its JSON content, and returns the array of jobs. If the file doesn't exist, return an empty array.
steps.hint: Use fs.readFileSync to read the file and JSON.parse to convert the content. Wrap the reading in a try-catch block to handle missing files.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named readExistingJobs that safely reads and parses the job tracking file, returning an array of jobs or an empty array.
successCriteria: The readExistingJobs function is defined, uses fs.readFileSync and JSON.parse, handles missing files with try-catch, and returns an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function handles both cases: when the file exists and when it doesn't.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't seem to work correctly. Check that you're reading the file, parsing JSON, and handling errors properly.

steps.instruction: Create a function named writeJobsToFile that takes an array of jobs as a parameter and writes it to the tracking file as JSON.
steps.hint: Use fs.writeFileSync with JSON.stringify to write the jobs array to the file path constant. Wrap it in a try-catch block for error handling.
steps.expectedOutcome: A writeJobsToFile function that accepts a jobs array and writes it to the tracking file as JSON with error handling.
successCriteria: The writeJobsToFile function is defined, takes a jobs parameter, uses fs.writeFileSync with JSON.stringify, and includes try-catch error handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it includes JSON.stringify and error handling with try-catch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't match the required structure. It should accept a jobs array, write to the file, and handle errors.

steps.title: Create duplicate detection logic
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'isDuplicateJob' that takes a job object as a parameter and checks if a job with the same id already exists in the tracking file.
steps.hint: You'll need to read the existing jobs using the helper function you created earlier, then compare the new job's id with each existing job's id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that can detect duplicate jobs by comparing their IDs with existing jobs in the file.
successCriteria: The isDuplicateJob function is defined, takes a job parameter, reads existing jobs, and returns true if a duplicate is found.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it properly reads existing jobs and compares the job IDs. Check if you're using the readExistingJobs helper function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't correctly implemented. Remember to read existing jobs and compare the new job's id with each existing job's id.

steps.instruction: Create a function named addJob that takes a job object as a parameter, reads existing jobs, checks for duplicates using isDuplicateJob, adds the new job if it's not a duplicate, and writes the updated jobs back to file using writeJobsToFile.
steps.hint: The function should call readExistingJobs to get current jobs, use isDuplicateJob to check if the new job exists, push the job to the array if it's unique, then call writeJobsToFile with the updated array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named addJob is created that orchestrates reading, duplicate checking, and writing operations.
successCriteria: The addJob function is defined, calls readExistingJobs, uses isDuplicateJob for duplicate checking, pushes the new job to the array if unique, and calls writeJobsToFile with the updated array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
